exercises.prompt: You are given cards, an array of Yu-Gi-Oh! card records, each an object { name, archetype, atk, def, level } — for example { name: 'Dark Magician', archetype: 'Dark Magician', atk: 2500, def: 2100, level: 7 }. Implement countByArchetype(cards) so it returns an object mapping each archetype to how many cards belong to it — { archetype: count }. countByArchetype(cards) is {'Blue-Eyes': 2, 'Dark Magician': 3, 'Red-Eyes': 2, 'Elemental HERO': 4, 'Kuriboh': 2, 'Archfiend': 2}. An empty array returns an empty object {}.

hints: This is a frequency tally keyed by each card's archetype field.
Walk the cards bumping counts[c.archetype] = (counts[c.archetype] || 0) + 1.
Loop the cards updating counts[c.archetype] = (counts[c.archetype] || 0) + 1, then return counts — || 0 seeds each archetype the first time it appears.

hints: Keep only the cards whose level matches, then project each survivor down to its name.

hints: Keep the cards that meet or beat the threshold, then project each to its name.
The test is atk >= threshold — greater-than-or-equal, so a card exactly at the threshold is included.
return cards.filter(c => c.atk >= threshold).map(c => c.name) — using >= is why the three 2500-atk cards appear when threshold is 2500, where a strict > would drop them.

hints: Fold the cards down to the single strongest one, carrying the current leader, then read its name.
reduce with no initial value seeds the accumulator with the first card; each step keeps whichever of best and c has the larger atk.
return cards.reduce((best, c) => (c.atk > best.atk ? c : best)).name — the strict > keeps the earlier card on a tie, so the first 3000-atk Blue-Eyes wins.
